fact: The Assembly of the Republic's Standing Commission (CPAR) decided on 2026-10-01 to place a draft law on Personal Data Protection on the initial 35-item agenda of the 4th Ordinary Session opening 2026-10-28.
A roundtable in Maputo reported on 2026-09-03 (held the previous week) discussed a forthcoming Personal Data Protection Law; the report gives no stage of the bill and no submission date.

The UNECA/GIZ/AU Commission inception report dated 19 June 2025 says Mozambique has not enacted a comprehensive data protection law but has drafted a Data Protection Bill, and lists a pending data protection law as a challenge.
The inception report states that Mozambique has no data regulatory authority, though INTIC, INCM, INAGE and CEDSIF impliedly oversee parts of data governance.
TechHive Advisory reviewed a comprehensive draft Personal Data Protection Law for Mozambique; the review gives no date for the draft, so its published date is used.

fact: The draft law designates the existing Regulatory Authority for ICT to take the role of National Authority for the Protection of Personal Data (ANPD), alongside a National Council chaired by the Prime Minister; the review's published date is used as no other date is given.

fact: The World Bank and African Development Bank diagnostic of Mozambique's data governance, with evidence updated to spring 2025, refers to the government's preparation of a draft Data Protection Law and recommends that it adopt a data protection law, so none was in force; the document gives no date for the draft, so its 2025-12-09 publication date and spring 2025 evidence cut-off are used.
The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records that Mozambique ratified or acceded to the Malabo Convention on 2019-12-02 and deposited its instrument on 2020-01-21.

DLA Piper states that Mozambique has no specific data protection or privacy legislation, only sector laws imposing some privacy obligations and a cybersecurity bill under discussion; the guide gives no event date, so its last-modified date of 17 February 2026 is used.
DLA Piper lists Resolution no. 5/2019 of 20 June as ratifying the African Union Convention on Cybersecurity and Personal Data Protection for Mozambique.

INTIC President Lourino Chemane said on 5 December 2025 that, by plan, the data protection law document would be presented to the Cabinet for approval by June 2026, and the minister said the government expected to have the law ready by then.
The World Bank restructuring paper says that as of October 2025 the Data Protection Act had not been approved by Cabinet or submitted to Parliament, and calls the Data Protection Law still pending.

The World Bank restructuring paper says the Data Protection Office is not yet established, which prevents its operationalisation, and the project envelope for it was cut from US$18m to US$11m; the date is the paper's October 2025 status.

Communications and Digital Transformation Minister Americo Muchanga said on 22 July 2026 that Mozambique is consolidating its legal framework with a future personal data protection law still in preparation, and asked industry to take part in the discussion before approval.
